description: 1D six-equation-capable two-fluid. HARD CONSTRAINT: must trace back to the OUTRAM-FOAM 3D reference (op-2kk), not invented independently. Process: OUTRAM-FOAM -> validate 3D -> reduce dimensionality -> implement 1D. Same physics, different dimensionality. DoD: theory+verification+benchmark+unit-safe uom.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
1-D SIX-EQUATION SOLVER IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 under op-62vf. crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/two_fluid.rs is no longer a scaffold: step() marches.

DoD status against this bead's 'theory + verification + benchmark + unit-safe uom':
  theory      DONE. Module docs carry the full six-equation set, the derivation of the pressure equation from the volume constraint, and the regularisation with its provenance.
  verification DONE. 18 tests in two_fluid_tests.rs: the 2x2 block algebra against closed forms, both vanishing-phase limits (exact to 1e-15 at alpha = 0), the no-slip limit (1/K_d asymptote to 3 figures), exact mass conservation, a well-balanced check that returns identical zeros, the interfacial energy identity to 4.15e-11, monotone thermal relaxation over five decades, and a regression for a phase-extinction bug.
  benchmark   NOT DONE, and BLOCKED -- see the low-void bead. Edwards-O'Brien starts 57 K subcooled, which is exactly the regime the solver refuses.
  unit-safe uom DONE at the API boundary; the marching loop is raw f64 in strict SI with every boundary documented, matching drift_flux.

TRACE-BACK CONSTRAINT HONOURED, with one stated exception. Drag comes from outram_foam_multiphase::two_fluid::DragModel and heat transfer from outram_foam_multiphase::heat_transfer::InterfacialHeatTransfer, both through super::interfacial rather than reimplemented. The exception is VIRTUAL MASS: InterfacialForce::VirtualMass upstream is an unported scaffold returning NotImplemented, so the formula is transcribed locally from OpenFOAM dispersedVirtualMassModel.C:51-67 via the source study, with the deviation stated in its doc comment and a bead filed to port it properly.

ALSO CORRECTED: two_fluid.rs used to claim the 3-D reference 'has no interfacial heat-transfer closure at all -- it is isothermal -- so there is nothing to trace back to'. That became false when outram_foam_multiphase::heat_transfer was ported; the module docs now say so explicitly rather than leaving a doc that misdescribes the codebase.

title: 1D Two-Fluid (reduced from OUTRAM-FOAM Stage 2)

description:
THE blocker. tuas_boussinesq_solver spawns OS threads in LIBRARY code (not tests) in exactly the two pre_built_components htgr_sim_v1 uses: shell_and_tube_heat_exchanger (41 sites, e.g. calculation.rs:1464, preprocessing.rs:1199) and one_d_solid_structure (2). std::thread::spawn compiles but PANICS AT RUNTIME on wasm32-unknown-unknown.

The pattern is spawn-then-join-immediately, so serialising changes nothing numerically.

Three options, recommendation is (1) then (2) as follow-up:
1. cfg(target_arch=wasm32) sequential equivalents beside each spawn/join. Mechanical, low-risk, easy to review.
2. Refactor spawn/join into one small internal abstraction with native+wasm impls, so 43 sites become 1. Cleaner, bigger diff, and the shape a future rayon-on-wasm story would want.
3. wasm-bindgen-rayon + SharedArrayBuffer. Real browser threads, but needs COOP/COEP cross-origin-isolation headers, which plain GitHub Pages cannot set. NOT recommended for a demo whose whole point is 'open a link'.

Acceptance: a native test asserting the threaded and serial paths agree BIT-FOR-BIT. They should, given join-immediately semantics; if they do not, that is a finding about TUAS worth its own bead. GH #39 Phase 3.
title: Phase 3: TUAS serial fallback for the 43 thread::spawn sites on wasm

description:
tampines::gas_phase landed 2026-08-11 (op-jyyp.12) with three working component models -- GasDuct (Churchill friction + Gnielinski/Dittus-Boelter heat transfer, low-Mach compressible), KtaBed (KTA 3102.3 packed-bed pressure drop) and Circulator (idealised fixed-rise/fixed-ratio compression). They are deliberately NOT wired into src/components/, which bead op-ql8 owns.

Interface notes for whoever does that wiring:

1. PipeBackend (components/pipe.rs) is an enum over stateful fluid ARRAYS (SinglePhaseFluidArray, CompressibleFluidArray, TampinesSteamArray, InsulatedFluidComponent). gas_phase::GasDuct is a different shape: it is stateless plain-data geometry plus a one-shot steady solve(mass_flow, T_in, p_in, boundary) -> GasDuctResult. It is NOT a drop-in PipeBackend variant.
   Suggested resolution: add a separate `SteadyGas(GasDuct)` variant, and accept that Pipe's methods split into a transient path (the array backends) and a steady path (this one), rather than forcing GasDuct to carry cell state it does not have.

2. KtaBed has no components/ counterpart at all -- a porous/packed-bed component struct would be new. It composes cleanly with crate::pebble_bed::zbs::ZbsBed (friction side + conduction side of the same bed).

3. Circulator is the gas analogue of components::Pump. Pump is currently a NotYetImplemented wrapper, so the cleanest move is probably a `PumpBackend` enum with a `GasCirculator(Circulator)` variant, mirroring PipeBackend.

4. All three take/return uom types and use crate::TampinesError, so error and unit conventions already match components/.

5. gas_phase exposes two public uom aliases -- MassFlux (kg/(m^2 s)) and PressureGradient (Pa/m) -- because uom ships no named types for those dimensions. If components/ needs them, re-export rather than redefining; note outram-park-digital-twin-engine/src/htr10/kta.rs independently defines identical aliases.

Blocked on op-ql8 finishing the NotYetImplemented wrapper pass.
title: tampines components/: add gas-phase variants so gas_phase components slot into the Pipe/Pump component layer

description:
Follow-up from op-jyyp.16 (ZBS test suite written 2026-08-11).

Two items in crates/tampines/src/pebble_bed/zbs.rs need a HUMAN with sources in hand; neither can be closed by running code:

1. TRANSCRIPTION. The dimensionless ZBS form (B, k_r, N, k_c, k_eff/k_f) was implemented without page-level access to the printed originals. The new test suite verifies the k_r -> 0 degeneration to the classic Zehner-Schlunder closed form to 1.398e-16 relative, but that is an ALGEBRAIC cross-check of the same expression regrouped -- it cannot detect a transcription error in the source equations. Needs checking against van Antwerpen, du Toit & Rousseau, Nucl. Eng. Des. 240 (2010) 1803-1818, eqs (12)-(16) (proprietary tier). Until then the module stays at Prototype in the V&V pipeline.

2. UNCITED CLAIM. The module docs previously asserted that stagnant-helium graphite beds measure order 1-2 W/(m K) at ambient in SANA/HTTU-class experiments, used as support for the finding that the VTB 18-point table is not reproducible. On 2026-08-11 this was flagged in-file as an uncited recollection, NOT checked against any source. It must be either given a real citation (source, tier, URL/DOI, date accessed per DATA_POLICY.md) or removed. None of the measured numbers in the module depend on it.

Also note the near-wall profile coefficients (1.36, 5.0) in ZbsBed::wall_region_porosity carry the same unverified-coefficient caveat.

Context: the VTB table mismatch itself is already tracked as op-jvua. Measured 2026-08-11: model/table ratio 0.176932 at 300 K rising to 0.644374 at 2000 K; reproducing the 300 K point would need k_f = 3.8367 W/(m K), 23.99x helium at 300 K / 6 MPa.
title: tampines zbs: human transcription check vs van Antwerpen (2010) eqs (12)-(16), and cite-or-drop the SANA/HTTU claim

description:
Two related changes to the HTR-10 kinetics, both AFTER the rustfmt standardisation pass. Maintainer, 2026-08-12.

=== 1. CONTROL-ROD INSERTION, NOT A REACTIVITY SLIDER ===

'you shouldn't give me a slider for reactivity, but rather control rod insertion. This should be similar to fhr_sim_v2'

Today panels.rs exposes external reactivity directly, which is a DERIVED quantity no operator ever sets. An operator moves rods; reactivity is what results. An operator-facing twin should expose the real control.

Follow fhr_sim_v2, which already has control-rod insertion fractions driving its kinetics (see its side panel and prke_backend).

WHAT HTR-10 ACTUALLY HAS, from IAEA-TECDOC-1382 (ingested):
  - 10 control rods, IN THE SIDE REFLECTOR, not in the core. They drop by
    gravity for shutdown.
  - 7 small absorber ball units, also in the side reflector, as the second
    independent shutdown system.
  - Rod worth: TECDOC-1382 carries CONTROL ROD WORTH as one of its three
    benchmark cases, so a sourced worth curve is available rather than invented.

TOOL ALREADY IN THE WORKSPACE: crates/teh-o-prke/src/control_rod_feedback.rs has
obtain_rod_worth_cylinder, a Lamarsh S-curve worth
rho(x) = rho_H * [x/H - sin(2*pi*x/H)/(2*pi)]. That is the right shape — worth
accumulates fastest near mid-insertion — and is already unit-tested at half
insertion.

Note the widget library's reactor vessels already TAKE a rod insertion fraction
and draw the rods at depth, so the GUI half is largely wired: the vessel art
will show insertion once the control drives it.

=== 2. SOURCED FUEL-TEMPERATURE FEEDBACK COEFFICIENT ===

kinetics.rs:116 currently uses TemperatureCoefficient::new::<per_kelvin>(-4.0e-5),
an ILLUSTRATIVE value carried over from when this simulator was a generic
~200 MWth HTGR. Its own doc comment says so. The plant has since been rescaled to
the real HTR-10 (10 MWth, 4.3 kg/s) against TECDOC-1382, so this constant is now
the odd one out.

TECDOC-1382's three benchmark cases are initial criticality, CONTROL ROD WORTH,
and the TEMPERATURE COEFFICIENT — so the sourced coefficient is already in the
ingested document. Replace the invented value and cite it.

Watch for the sign and basis: a benchmark may quote a coefficient for fuel,
moderator or the whole core, and this model carries a SINGLE lumped fuel node.
Do not silently apply a whole-core coefficient to a fuel-only node — state which
was used and why.

=== ACCEPTANCE ===

Rod insertion drives reactivity through a worth curve; the reactivity slider is
gone from the operator panel; the feedback coefficient is sourced and cited; and
the Nordheim-Fuchs excursion remains self-limiting (negative alpha) with a test
proving a rod withdrawal produces a bounded power rise rather than a runaway.

Nordheim-Fuchs feedback itself is ALREADY PRESENT and correct — kinetics.rs
composes NordheimFuchsExactTimestepper with a five-group delayed bank under a
documented Lie split. This bead does not add it; it makes its inputs real.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Closed 2026-08-14 on the maintainer's report that control-rod sensitivity has been changed.

VERIFIABLE IN THE CODE: part 1 of this bead is done. The GUI commands control-rod INSERTION FRACTION, not reactivity -- HtgrSnapshot::control_rod_insertion_fraction (0.0 withdrawn to 1.0 inserted), clamped at the stops by crate::physics::control_rods, with reactivity published back as external_reactivity_dollars purely for display. Its doc comment states the design explicitly: 'reactivity is a consequence of rod position, not something commanded directly'. GUI_INITIAL_ROD_INSERTION opens near the critical position implied by the published bank worth.

NOT VERIFIED BY ME: the feedback coefficient's sourcing, which was part 2 of this bead. I have not checked what value is now used or what it is sourced from. If that half is still open, it wants its own bead rather than living on in a closed one.

title: htgr_sim_v1 kinetics: control-rod insertion control + sourced feedback coefficient

description:
Surfaced by the wasm audit (op-okqo.5) on 2026-09-04.

outram-park-mpi had 'const COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40', a compile-time overflow on ANY 32-bit target. It was caught by wasm32 — but armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android are also 32-bit and would have failed identically.

The workspace CLAUDE.md Android rule says every crate's non-GUI library must compile for 'aarch64-linux-android and the armv7/x86_64 emulator targets', but the acceptance command it gives names only aarch64:
    cargo check -p <crate> --all-targets --target aarch64-linux-android

So the 32-bit Android targets are claimed as supported but are not in the gate, and at least one crate proves they were not being checked.

Do: run cargo check --all-targets against armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android across the workspace, record how many crates fail and why, then either (a) fix them and add both to the documented acceptance command, or (b) narrow the CLAUDE.md claim to the targets actually gated. Option (b) is a legitimate answer — what is not acceptable is the current gap between the stated claim and the checked reality.

Expect more width assumptions specifically: grep for '1 <<' on usize, 'as usize' on 64-bit quantities, and size_of::<usize>().
title: Android rule: the 32-bit targets (armv7, i686) appear never to have been built
